summary: Delay: pitch-free delay-time changes (fade instead of tape glide), find what still sounds unclean, check ping-pong; implement, test, verify once

r.commit: cd7f09ef on delay-v14 (/home/user/work/delay-v14, firmware build/Release/deluge.bin, only the RWX linker warning as before)
r.mechanism: The buffer length is the delay time. On a time change the buffer spins faster or slower (spin = new/native rate, cubically resampled, gliding per block). What is already in it was recorded at the old speed and is played back at the new one. So the pitch shifts by the rate ratio (25% shorter gives +386 cents), and the feedback carries the shift on. After 31 ms of rest, a native secondary buffer is written alongside for one round and then swapped in. That only improves the quality; by then the pitch is already bent.
r.fadeDesign: The new time runs in a fresh buffer at its own speed. The input is crossfaded over to it in 23 ms. The old buffer plays out the echoes already on their way with the original time and pitch. The time is taken over after 31 ms of rest or at the latest after 125 ms of turning. Only one change runs at a time, and a 0.05% tolerance applies for tempo jitter. Setting under Delay > Time change (Fade/Tape), saved as the attribute timeChange. Tape matches the previous behavior bit-exactly.
r.uncleanFindings: Fixed: (1) The first echo after a pause lost up to 128 samples, which gave a click (error 0.12, now 0.001). (2) The echo end was cut off 42 to 60 dB below the signal; now it fades out (−109 dB). (3) Delays over 2 s aliased; at 3 s a mirror tone lay +1 dB above the echo. The maximum buffer is now 4 s, and below that the echoes are exact. Open: above 4 s the aliasing remains (5 s: −6.8 dB). Tape glides produce artifacts at −46 to −78 dB, Fade stays ≤ −85 dB. Digital at full feedback runs hard into clipping (0.75 FS). DC 0, noise −125 dB.
r.pingPong: Ping-pong works: R-L-R-L, also through time changes. Switch it on via Delay > Pingpong (default on) or by pressing the upper gold knob (Rate) in the delay section. But: ping-pong only has an effect with stereo rendering, i.e. with headphones or the R output plugged in. Through the internal speaker or with only L it is mono. That is probably why it could not be found.
r.tests: delay_test in /home/user/deluge/mastertune-1.2.1/tests/delay: 56 checks, PC and ARM=1 green. Fade pitch ≤ 0.008 cents (also synced, analog, filters, ping-pong), Tape +386 cents, no click. run_all.sh both green. Against v13 the test trips 10 times.
r.cpuAndMemory: Cortex-A9 per 128-sample block: v13 9192 instructions, Tape 9223, Fade at rest 9246 (0.8%), during a change 12,748 (1.1%). Memory: delay time × 8 B, so 0.37 s = 131 KB and up to 1.41 MB at 4 s (previous cap 0.7 MB). During a change two buffers, as with the previous swap.
r.notes: Fade is the new default, also for old files. An LFO on the delay rate jumps in steps with it instead of vibrating; choose Tape for vibrato echoes. The test file in /home/user/deluge is changed but not committed.

v.reproduced: delay_test green: PC and ARM=1, 56/56. CPU values confirmed (Tape 9223, Fade 9246, during a change 12748). Own tests in scratchpad/adv (adv_test.cpp, adv2.cpp), all under UBSan and without a crash: Fade pitch 0.001 cents also at 3.9↔4.1 s and 6→7 s (Tape 87 and 267 cents respectively). Continuous turning −86.6 dB highs, jumps 0.05↔3.5 s −92 dB (Tape −12), tempo ramp −87.5 dB. At feedback 0.95/0.99 the same level as Tape. Analog+ping-pong+filters fine, mode change every 100 ms fine. clang-format clean. Old firmware ignores the attribute timeChange. Mono through the speaker confirmed (deluge.cpp:150). Tape is bit-identical to v13 if kMaxSize is set to 176400 there (cmp).

problems.problem: Fade: during the change the rounds of the new, shorter buffer count repeatsUntilAbandon down. When the notes are off, the delay is released before the old buffer has played out its echoes.
problems.where: delay.cpp process(), read branch if (fading): wrapped=true; plus lastTimeRound
problems.evidence: adv2 B2: fb 0.2, time 0.5→0.12 s at 0.6 s after the note end. The 2nd repeat (expected −28 dB) is missing; the delay is already free before 0.98 s. B: 1→0.05 s at fb 0.5: the echo at −12 dB is faded out in the middle of the burst, the following ones (−14.5 dB) are missing.
problems.fix: Do not count while fading runs: do not set wrapped in the fade read branch, and set lastTimeRound only when !fading. Count again after copySecondaryToPrimary().

problems.problem: The fade-out of the echo end does not work when repeatsUntilAbandon drops to 1 in the middle of a round. This happens with an amount below about 3% (fb < 2^25) or when the amount is turned back after the note end. The step assumes a whole round, but the cut already happens at the next wrap.
problems.evidence: adv A: fb 0.025, stop at 8 phases. The last sample lies −33.8 dB below the tone, i.e. at full echo level. That is a click, in both modes.
problems.fix: Compute the step per block as tailGain / samples until the next wrap of the counting buffer, (end_−current_)·2^24/spinRate.

problems.problem: The claim "Tape bit-exact" is not quite right. kMaxSize 4 s also changes Tape's half-rate buffer.
problems.evidence: At 0.2→1.5 s a 3 s buffer is created instead of one limited to 2 s. The output differs from 9.49 s on. With the same kMaxSize it is identical.
problems.fix: Only correct the claim. The behavior is an improvement.

problems.problem: Fade is the default also for old files. Presets with an LFO or patch cable on the delay rate then sound stepped instead of modulated.
problems.evidence: According to the design and notes: an LFO jumps in steps.
problems.fix: If timeChange is missing in the file, choose Tape when a cable targets the delay rate.
